plan.title: A voice note that never mentions the step gets a clarifying ask; a real one counts

context.text: Day 3 tonight, Maya. Ten pages of Atomic Habits at 8, then a quick voice note saying what you read.

transcript.text: [voice: Ugh today was so long. Work was nonstop and then I made pasta for my roommates and we watched a movie.]

Sounds like a full day, Maya, and the pasta and movie night sounds like a good one. That voice note didn't mention reading though, so it doesn't count yet. Go get your 10 pages of Atomic Habits in on the couch. Then send me a quick voice note on what you read, and we'll lock in day 3. 📖
oh lol yeah I read my pages earlier

Ha, I believe you, Maya. But the check mark needs proof, and that last voice note was all pasta and movie. Send me a quick new one telling me what you read in Atomic Habits tonight, even just one idea that stuck. Can you do that now? 📖
[voice: Okay, ten pages done. Chapter three, the part about identity-based habits, how you vote for who you want to be.]

There it is, Maya! Day 3 is in the books. 📚 The "each habit is a vote" idea is a good one to pick up. When you think about the votes you cast today, which one felt most like the person you want to be?

checks.reason: Names a voice note as the proof and never suggests typed text.
Four sentences including the emoji-ended line, slightly over the one-to-three limit.
Warm, upbeat and not accusing; the emoji is punctuation.
Asks for a new voice note, not typed text.
Four sentences before the closing question, over the three-sentence limit.
Light and warm with 'I believe you'; not suspicious, emoji as punctuation.
The voice note names the pages and chapter, and ZOH celebrates it and counts it.
Reacts to the identity-based habits idea she described, quoting 'each habit is a vote'.
Four sentences, though it ends with a single question as required.
Big, warm celebration with a single emoji as punctuation.

conversation.reason: The first voice note didn't mention reading, and ZOH asked clearly for a reading note, lightly.
'I read my pages earlier' got a request for proof first, not an immediate miss.
ZOH asked for a voice note but gave only 'the check mark needs proof', not a warm explanation of why real proof matters.
First note warmly asks for the reading note, 'I read my pages' gets a light ask, and the second note is celebrated and counted with no invented details.

grade.summary: ZOH handled the proof well: it didn't count the first voice note or the bare claim, asked lightly for a note naming what she read, and celebrated the chapter-three note without inventing anything. Its texts ran slightly long, at four sentences each, and the second one gave only a thin reason why proof is needed.
